extracted.intended_audience: AoPS Wiki contributors / users writing problem solutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing problem and solution pages on the Art of Problem Solving Wiki: formatting templates, LaTeX usage, tone/level of detail, wikification/linking, images, and how to present final answers and remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem/solution page template
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem/solution pages have simple template formats to follow: == Problem == <PROBLEM GOES HERE> ... == Solution == <SOLUTION GOES HERE> == See also == {{SUCCESSION box|year=YYYY|num-b=NUMB|num-a=NUMA}} [[Category:DIFFICULTY SUBJECT Problems]]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The items in caps refer respectively to the problem statement, multiple choice answers format (if applicable), the solution, the year, the appropriate succession box, the number before this question (NUMB), the number after the question (NUMA), the difficulty (Introductory/Intermediate/Olympiad), and the subject (Algebra/Trigonometry/Number Theory/Combinatorics/Geometry). More details can be found at A:CPS. Succession template box documentation is on their respective pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-choice answer formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple choice, include answers in the specified inline format:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: $\mathrm{(A)}\ ANSWER \qquad \mathrm{(B)}\ ANSWER \qquad \mathrm{(C)}\ ANSWER \qquad \mathrm{(D)}\ ANSWER \qquad \mathrm{(E)}\ ANSWER$ so choices are clearly presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LaTeX for math
rubrics_metrics.description: Place all variables, numbers, and equations relevant to the problem in LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX formats math and distinguishes it from text. Important equations should be written outside the text and given space by centering the equation (use the display math delimiters). Examples of commonly used commands on the page: \frac{a}{b}, \pi, \Longrightarrow, \boxed{5}, \text{TEXT GOES HERE}. Use align or eqnarray environments for multiple equations, e.g. \begin{align*} x &= 2 \cdot 2 + 2 \\ x &= 4 + 2 \\ x &= 6 \end{align*} or \begin{eqnarray*} x + y &=& x-y \\ 2x &=& -2y \\ x &=& -y \end{eqnarray*}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center and separate important equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Important equations should be written outside of the text and given space by centering the equation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use display math (centered equations) so they stand out from prose. This improves readability and emphasizes key steps or results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: clarity and appropriate level of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions should be clear and concise while still being easy to follow for students with less experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit basic arithmetic and other trivial steps to avoid clutter; the reader should be able to carry out trivial arithmetic themselves. What counts as trivial varies by problem type (e.g., AMC 8 vs olympiad). Balance detail so the solution remains accessible to a range of readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link all used theorems/results (Wikification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use wiki links to connect the solution to theorems or results which are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to link to all theorems or other results used so readers unfamiliar with them can easily access the information. Syntax: [[LINK]] and to change displayed text: [[LINK|TEXT HERE]].

rubrics_metrics.name: Casework formatting (bullets and numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: For casework, use wiki bulleting to organize separate cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '*' to create bullet points for cases: Case 1: Case 2: For problems with an established number of cases, convert bullets into numbers using '#'. This helps indent and distinguish separate cases visually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use images for geometric/illustrative solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Images are often useful in illustrating solutions, especially geometry questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request an image, add {{image}} at the location and optionally describe the requested image in a comment. Asymptote (vector graphics language) images can be embedded directly using <asy> ... </asy> tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting/embedding Asymptote images
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote images can be embedded into articles using the <asy> tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include <asy> ... </asy> with Asymptote code for vector graphics when appropriate. If you cannot create the image yourself, use {{image}} to request creation and describe the nature of the image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box the final answer for open-ended questions
rubrics_metrics.description: For open-ended questions, separate the answer from the rest of the math by boxing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \boxed{TEXT} to highlight the final answer so it is immediately visible to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include remarks or alternate solutions when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If appropriate, remark on aspects of the proof or suggest alternate solutions or extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding remarks or noting alternate approaches can help readers understand the proof's context or see different techniques; do this judiciously for open-ended problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Category pages should follow the format [[Category:DIFFICULTY SUBJECT Problems]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace DIFFICULTY with Introductory/Intermediate/Olympiad and SUBJECT with Algebra/Trigonometry/Number Theory/Combinatorics/Geometry so pages are categorized consistently.
